blocks.text: Jesus’ statement that “salvation is from the Jews” places his own mission and the story of salvation within the Jewish people and Scripture. It should not be read as erasing Jewish identity or treating Samaritans as inferior. Likewise, the Gospel’s references to “Jews” have context-sensitive meanings; they should not be turned into a description of a single hostile ethnic group. The Samaritan woman is presented as a sustained conversation partner and then as a witness whose testimony leads others to Jesus. Although Jesus names her marital history, the passage does not say that she was adulterous or a prostitute, so readers should not add that label to her story.
